newsitem.title: USA: U.S. receives bids in first round of new SPR sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. receives bids in first round of new SPR sale.

text.p: The U.S. Defense Fuel Supply Center received bids Monday for crude oil offered in the first round of its new auction from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, a DFSC spokeswoman said.
She declined to say how many bids were received or when best and final offers were due. Awards will be announced if and when they are made, an Energy Department official said.

The government is offering up to 15 million barrels of light sour crude and 370,000 barrels of sweet crude in its new sale, which was ordered by Congress to raise $220 million for running the SPR in the 1997 fiscal year, which began October 1.
The current auction will continue until the government raises $220 million, with fresh bids due every two weeks.
This is the third time since January that the government has turned to the emergency stockpile to help trim the budget deficit.
